title: Scalar antiholomorphic coefficient forms and their Dolbeault differential
statement: Use the usual fields $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field] and the conjugate Wirtinger derivative $\partial_{\bar z_j}=\tfrac12(\partial_{x_j}+i\partial_{y_j})$ [def-sfb-kahler-coordinate-data]. For $n,q\geq0$ and an open $U\subset\mathbf C^n$, a scalar $(0,q)$ coefficient form is a family $(f_J:U\to\mathbf C)_J$ indexed by increasing $q$-tuples in $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, denoting $\sum_J f_J\,d\bar z_J$. It is smooth when every coefficient is real smooth on $U$. For $q>n$ there are no indices, hence only the zero form. Restriction to $V\subset U$ is restriction of each coefficient. Define its Dolbeault differential by the coefficient formula $(\bar\partial\alpha)_K=\sum_{r=0}^{q}(-1)^r\partial_{\bar z_{K_r}} f_{K\setminus K_r}$ for every increasing $(q+1)$-tuple $K$; equivalently $\bar\partial\alpha=\sum_{j,J}(\partial_{\bar z_j}f_J)d\bar z_j\wedge d\bar z_J$. Coefficients are actual functions on $U$; zero extensions are used only inside derivatives and smoothness tests within $U$, so no regularity across the boundary is imposed.

source.place: Demailly, I §3.C, formulas (3.14)--(3.17), printed pp.23--24; read https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf in this sandbox.

reviewed_lean.note: Both item theorems match the node clause by clause: open U, a in U, degree q+1, smooth, closed gives an open V with a in V inside U and a smooth degree-q beta on V with dbar(beta) = alpha restricted to V; the degree-0 iff is complex differentiability on open U. New def node def-sfb-scalar-dolbeault-forms: increasing-tuple coefficients (Fin q ↪o Fin n) on U, ContDiffOn R infinity, restriction, and dbar with the (-1)^r deletion sign via succAboveOrderEmb.comp (= K composed with succAbove r), reusing wirtingerBarPartial (dx + i dy)/2; signs and normalization verified. No duplicate in Mathlib, live or side-live (HermitianDolbeaultData and Q143's DolbeaultSheafData are different settings). Edge cases n=0, q>n and empty U are fine.
